Isaiah had called it a house of prayer for all people; Jeremiah had asked, is this house become a den of robbers in your eyes? The trade occupied the court of the Gentiles, the only place the nations could pray, and did it, on the gospel's account, for profit under the priests' patronage. Driven out with a whip. The chief priests sought how they might destroy him for it. Zechariah's last verse hangs over the scene: in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite, the trafficker, in the house of the Lord of hosts.

name: The woman taken in adultery
text: Adultery, in the very act. The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery and set her in the midst: Moses commanded that such should be stoned; what sayest thou? They said it to tempt him. He wrote on the ground, and then: he that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. Hers was capital under Leviticus 20 and Deuteronomy 22, and the accusers were right about the statute. But the same statute requires the man, absent here, and Deuteronomy 17 requires the witnesses to cast the first stones on their own testimony. Christ put the witnesses to the test the law itself imposes. Convicted by their own conscience, they went out one by one, beginning at the eldest. With no witness remaining there was no case: hath no man condemned thee? Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more. Spared, and commanded.

name: Zacchaeus
text: Extortion as chief of the publicans. A rich chief tax-collector of Jericho climbed a sycamore to see Jesus and was called down by name. Standing in his house he said: the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold. The publican's trade as commonly practiced: assessment by false accusation and extortion, which Leviticus 6 classes with theft and fraud. Fourfold was the law's rate for a stolen sheep, the highest ordinary restitution, and Zacchaeus chose it for himself. This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham. The restitution was not the price of the salvation but its evidence: fruits meet for repentance, the very thing John had told the publicans to bring.

name: Zacharias
text: Not believing the words of the angel Gabriel, and asking for a sign. A righteous priest, walking in all the commandments blameless, was told at the altar of incense that his prayer was heard. He answered that he was old and his wife well stricken in years. He came out of the temple unable to speak, and stayed so until the day he wrote, His name is John. Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years. The angel answering said, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings. And, behold, thou shalt be dumb, and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall be performed, because thou believest not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season. The judgment was bounded exactly to the promise: when the child was circumcised and named, his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.

name: Joseph, the husband of Mary
text: A just man; doing as the angel of the Lord bade him, four times, without a word recorded. Betrothed to a woman found with child, and a just man, he meant to put her away privily rather than make her a public example. An angel told him in a dream whose the child was and he took her, and knew her not till she had brought forth. He was told to flee to Egypt and went by night; told to return, and returned; warned, and turned aside to Galilee. Scripture records no word he spoke, only what he did. Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt. Every year his parents went to Jerusalem at the feast of the passover. And he did all things according to the law of the Lord: the circumcision on the eighth day, the presentation, the pair of turtledoves. Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Jesus: for he shall save his people from their sins. The blessing on him is the charge itself: the Son of God was subject unto him, and grew up under his roof in Nazareth, and was called the carpenter's son. Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child's life.

name: Mary of Bethany
text: Sitting at his feet to hear his word; anointing his body aforehand to the burying. While her sister served, she sat at his feet and heard, and he called it the good part that would not be taken from her. Six days before the passover she broke an alabaster box of spikenard, very precious, over his head and feet and wiped them with her hair. The disciples called it waste. He called it a memorial for the whole world. Mary sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word. Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. Some had indignation: why was this waste of the ointment made? for it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and given to the poor. Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her. Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me. She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying. Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

name: Mary, the mother of Jesus
text: Be it unto me according to thy word; blessed is she that believed. A virgin of Nazareth, espoused, was told she would conceive by the Holy Ghost and bear the Son of the Highest, and that with God nothing shall be impossible. She answered, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. Elisabeth's word to her is the verdict: blessed is she that believed. Her own song says all generations shall call her blessed, and they have. And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. She arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste to Elisabeth. She kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart. When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord; as it is written in the law of the Lord. At Cana her word to the servants was the rule she lived by: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. She stood by the cross. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord. My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. From the cross her Son gave her to the disciple he loved, and from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

name: Simeon and Anna
text: Just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel; a widow who departed not from the temple, serving God with fastings and prayers night and day. An old man had been told by the Holy Ghost that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. He came by the Spirit into the temple the day a poor couple brought a forty-day-old child with a pair of turtledoves, took him in his arms, and asked to be let go in peace. A prophetess of eighty-four who had lived in the temple since her husband died came in that same hour and spoke of him to all that looked for redemption. Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. He came by the Spirit into the temple. Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; and she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. It was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: for mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem. Two who kept the law past the end of their strength were the first in the temple to know whom they had been waiting for.

name: The centurion of Capernaum
text: Loving the nation and building the synagogue; not counting himself worthy that the Lord should come under his roof: speak the word only. A Roman officer whose servant was dying sent the elders of the Jews, who pleaded that he was worthy, for he loved their nation and had built them a synagogue. He himself sent to say he was not worthy, and that a word would do, since he too was a man under authority. Christ marvelled, said he had not found so great faith in Israel, and the servant was healed in that hour. Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed. For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth. The elders of the Jews besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this: for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue. A Gentile who had done good to Israel and did not presume upon it. When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

name: The Samaritan leper who returned
text: One of ten: turning back to glorify God with a loud voice, and giving thanks at his feet. Ten lepers stood afar off and cried for mercy, and were sent to shew themselves to the priests as the law commands. As they went they were cleansed. Nine kept going. One, a Samaritan, turned back, fell on his face at his feet and gave thanks. He alone was told, thy faith hath made thee whole. And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. The other nine had obeyed the letter, going to the priests; this one came back to the one who had sent them. And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Ten were cleansed of leprosy; one went home whole.

name: The widow and her two mites
text: Casting in all that she had, even all her living. He sat over against the treasury and watched the rich cast in much. A poor widow threw in two mites, which make a farthing. He called his disciples to see it, and weighed it against everything else in the box: she had cast in more than they all. And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. The rich cast in of their abundance; she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. No one had asked her for it. And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: for all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living. Her gift is the standard by which every other gift in the temple that day was found smaller, and it is read in every generation since.

name: The woman with the issue of blood
text: Believing that if she might but touch his clothes she should be whole. Twelve years unclean under the law, spent to her last penny on physicians and worse for it, she came behind him in the press and touched the border of his garment. The flow dried up in the same hour. He turned and made her say it before everyone, and gave her the verdict in front of them: thy faith hath made thee whole. A certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse, when she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. When she saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him. And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague. Under the law her touch should have made him unclean; instead his made her clean, and she went home with the word that did it.

name: Zacharias and Elisabeth
text: Both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. A priest of the course of Abia and a daughter of Aaron, old, childless, and blameless in the whole law. Their prayer was heard at the altar of incense: a son, to be called John, filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb, who would go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias. Zacharias' unbelief at the news is its own case; the blessing stood. They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. He executed the priest's office before God in the order of his course, according to the custom of the priest's office. Elisabeth hid herself five months, saying, Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men. On the eighth day they circumcised the child, and against all their kindred named him as the angel had said. Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John. And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth. For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord. Her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her. Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost and prophesied: and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest. Christ's own verdict on their son: among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

name: Alexander the coppersmith
text: Doing Paul much evil; greatly withstanding his words. Named in Paul's last letter as a man to beware of. Whether he is the Alexander delivered to Satan with Hymenaeus for blasphemy, or the Alexander the Jews put forward in the Ephesian theatre, the sentence Paul leaves is the law's own: the Lord reward him according to his works. Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words. In the first letter to Timothy, Hymenaeus and Alexander had put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, and were delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme. The Lord reward him according to his works. Paul does not curse him in his own name; he cites the judgment already written for every man, and leaves Alexander under it. Timothy was told to beware of him, which is the church's share of the sentence: a man marked and avoided.

name: Ananias and Sapphira
text: Lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift. A couple sold property and gave part of the proceeds to the apostles while claiming it was the whole. The gift was never required; the lie was the offense. Each fell dead as it was exposed. They agreed together to keep back part of the price and present the rest as the full amount, a staged generosity meant to buy standing. Peter named it: not a lie to men but to God. Ananias fell dead at Peter's word; Sapphira, questioned three hours later and holding to the same story, fell dead as well. Great fear came on the whole church.

name: Ananias the high priest
text: Commanding Paul to be smitten on the mouth, contrary to the law, while sitting to judge him by the law. Paul had said one sentence to the council when the high priest ordered him struck. Paul answered as a prophet answers: God shall smite thee, thou whited wall; for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law? Then he withdrew the words toward the office, not the man. Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day. And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth. The law forbids condemning a man before he is heard, and forbids the judge to strike the accused; Ananias did both from the judgment seat. Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall. Told it was the high priest, he answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people. Scripture records the word spoken and not its performance; the office was honoured, the man was named, and the sentence was left with God.

name: Demas
text: Forsaking Paul, having loved this present world. Three times Demas appears in Paul's letters: a fellowlabourer sending greetings from Rome, then a name without a word, then a name with a verdict. Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica. Scripture says nothing more of him. He had stood with Paul in the first imprisonment, named with Luke among the fellowlabourers. In the second, with Paul's death near, he loved this present world and went to Thessalonica. The love of the world is named by John as the thing that cannot share a heart with the love of the Father. No sentence is written; the departure is the record. The law's word on the man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the apostle's on the friendship of the world, stand over the empty place where his name had been. Whether he came back is not told.

name: Demetrius and the silversmiths of Ephesus
text: Raising an uproar over lost trade under the colour of zeal for Diana. Demetrius called the craftsmen together and told them plainly what was at stake — Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth — then dressed the grievance up as danger to the temple of the great goddess. The city filled with confusion for two hours, and the townclerk sent them home. A certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen. He called them together and said that Paul had persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: so that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought, but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised. They were full of wrath, and the whole city was filled with confusion, and they caught Gaius and Aristarchus and rushed into the theatre. No sentence is recorded upon Demetrius. The townclerk appeased the people and gave the verdict the law would have given: ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly; for ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess. If Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another. And he warned them they were in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause — then dismissed the assembly.

name: Diotrephes
text: Loving the preeminence; prating against the apostle with malicious words; casting the brethren out of the church. John wrote to the church, but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, received him not. He spoke against the apostle with malicious words, refused to receive the traveling brethren himself, forbade those who would, and cast them out of the church. Pride in office, slander of an apostle, refusal of hospitality to the brethren, and excommunication used as a weapon. The law's word on the slanderer and on hospitality to strangers both apply; so does Christ's on those who would be greatest. Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth. The epistle records the charge and the intention; the sentence is not recorded. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.

name: Elymas the sorcerer
text: Withstanding the apostles; seeking to turn the deputy from the faith. At Paphos the proconsul Sergius Paulus sent for Barnabas and Saul to hear the word. Bar-jesus, a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet attached to his court, withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith. Paul, filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him. O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord? A sorcerer, forbidden by the law outright, using his influence to keep a ruler from the truth. The hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. Immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness, and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand. The deputy, seeing it, believed.

name: Felix the governor
text: Trembling at the judgment to come, hoping for a bribe, and leaving a man he knew to be innocent bound. Felix sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ, and as Paul reasoned of righteousness, temperance and judgment to come, he trembled. He put it off for a convenient season that never came, sent for Paul the oftener hoping for money, and after two years handed him on still bound, to do the Jews a pleasure. Felix heard Paul concerning the faith in Christ, and as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee. He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him. A judge who has heard the case, felt the truth of it, and wants paying to do what he already knows is right. Scripture records no sentence upon Felix. It records only what he did with the two years he was given: after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound. The convenient season is the whole of his judgment — he was moved, and asked for money, and was replaced, and the man he trembled before went to Rome in chains.

name: Herod Agrippa
text: Accepting worship due to God alone. Arrayed in royal robes, the king gave an oration and the crowd shouted that his was the voice of a god, not a man. He accepted the acclaim. The judgment was immediate and public. The sin was not the speech but the silence after it: he took to himself the honor owed to God, receiving worship he should have refused as Paul and Barnabas had refused it at Lystra. Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he gave not God the glory; he was eaten of worms and died. The contrast follows at once: but the word of God grew and multiplied.

name: Hymenaeus, Alexander, and Philetus
text: Making shipwreck of the faith; blasphemy; teaching that the resurrection is past already. Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander as men who put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. Hymenaeus and Philetus erred concerning the truth, saying the resurrection is past already, and overthrew the faith of some. Alexander the coppersmith did him much evil. Heresy that eats as doth a canker, spread inside the church by teachers. Titus gives the procedure: a man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject, knowing that he is subverted and sinneth, being condemned of himself. Delivered unto Satan, the apostolic form of putting out, with the stated aim of correction. Of Alexander Paul adds only: the Lord reward him according to his works.

name: Jezebel of Thyatira
text: Calling herself a prophetess; teaching the servants of God to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols. Christ's word to the angel of the church in Thyatira: thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants. He had given her space to repent of her fornication, and she repented not. The two things the apostles' council had bound on the Gentiles, abstinence from idol meats and from fornication, taught as liberty by a self-appointed prophetess, under a name that carried Ahab's queen with it. The church's toleration is charged against the church. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts.

name: Peter at Antioch
text: Dissembling: withdrawing from the Gentiles for fear of them of the circumcision. At Antioch Peter had eaten with the Gentiles until certain came from James; then he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews and even Barnabas were carried away with his dissimulation. Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. Hypocrisy in a pillar of the church, contradicting the vision God had given him at Joppa and the judgment he himself had argued at Jerusalem. Paul's charge: they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, and by the example compelled the Gentiles to live as do the Jews. A public rebuke before them all, and no more; the epistle records the correction and leaves the reconciliation to be inferred. Peter later commends Paul's letters as scripture. The case stands as the law's own rule for reproof: a trespass taken openly to the transgressor.

name: Saul of Tarsus
text: Persecuting the church; consenting to Stephen's death; compelling the saints to blaspheme. The young man at whose feet Stephen's killers laid their clothes made havock of the church, entering every house and haling men and women to prison, and set out for Damascus with letters to bind any he found of that way. A light from heaven and a voice met him on the road: why persecutest thou me? By his own later account: I persecuted this way unto the death; I punished them oft in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme; being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities. He was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and injurious. Three days blind and fasting in Damascus, then sight, baptism, and a commission. I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief. He calls himself the chief of sinners and the pattern of the longsuffering shown to them which should hereafter believe. Ananias was told he would be shown how great things he must suffer.

name: Simon Magus
text: Offering money for the gift of the Holy Ghost. A sorcerer of Samaria who had long bewitched the people and given out that he was some great one, Simon believed and was baptized under Philip. When he saw that the Spirit was given through the apostles' hands he offered them money for the same power. Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Peter names the state behind the offer: thy heart is not right in the sight of God; thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. A sorcerer's instinct, to buy power. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. Simon asked Peter to pray for him that none of these things come upon him, and the record ends there. His name became the word for buying office in the church.

name: The church in Pergamos
text: Holding among them the doctrine of Balaam and the doctrine of the Nicolaitans. Pergamos held fast his name and had not denied his faith, even where Satan's seat is, and in the days when Antipas was slain among them. The commendation stands; so does the charge. They kept the name and kept the teachers with it, and the sentence is suspended on one word: repent. I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith. But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which thing I hate. The fault is not that they taught it, but that they had them there. Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth. The sentence is pronounced and held: he which hath the sharp sword with two edges names the weapon he will use, and stays it on their repentance. To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.

name: The churches of Ephesus, Sardis, and Laodicea
text: Leaving the first love; a name to live while dead; lukewarm, and saying, I am rich. Three of the seven letters in the Revelation carry a sentence with a condition. Ephesus, sound in doctrine and patient, had left her first love and would lose her candlestick. Sardis had a name that it lived and was dead. Laodicea was neither cold nor hot, and was about to be spued out. Each was told what to do, and given time. Ephesus: I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Sardis: thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead; I have not found thy works perfect before God. Laodicea: thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot; thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. I will spue thee out of my mouth. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door, and knock. The sentence is written in full and stayed on the condition.

name: The Corinthian who had his father's wife
text: Fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles: a man with his father's wife. Paul heard that a member of the Corinthian church was living with his father's wife and that the church, instead of mourning, was puffed up. He judged the case in absence: deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus. Leviticus 18 and 20 and Deuteronomy 27 all name it, the last with a curse and the middle with death. Paul's rule follows the statute's shape: put away from among yourselves that wicked person. The church's tolerance was a second offense: a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump. Excommunicated by the assembly. The second letter shows the outcome: the punishment inflicted of many was sufficient, the man was overwhelmed with sorrow, and Paul urged them to forgive and comfort him and confirm their love toward him, lest Satan get an advantage. Banishment, then restoration on repentance.

name: The Corinthians at the Lord's supper
text: Eating and drinking unworthily; shaming them that have not. When the Corinthians came together it was not to eat the Lord's supper: every one took his own supper before another, one was hungry and another drunken, and the poor were shamed in the assembly of the church. Paul: what, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? Contempt for the assembly and for the brethren who had nothing, in the very meal that proclaimed the Lord's death. Whosoever shall eat this bread and drink this cup unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. Paul frames it as chastening: when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. The remedy: let a man examine himself, and tarry one for another.

name: The false witnesses against Stephen
text: Suborning witnesses and stirring up the council against a man they could not answer. They disputed with Stephen and were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. So they suborned men to say he had spoken blasphemous words against Moses and against God, stirred up the people and the elders, and set up false witnesses before the council. Losing an argument, they bought a charge. There arose certain of the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God. They stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, caught him, brought him to the council, and set up false witnesses. The law they claimed to defend requires the false witness to bear the penalty he sought for his brother. No sentence is recorded on them. They got what they came for: the council gnashed on Stephen with their teeth, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city and stoned him, and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. The last word spoken over them is the dying man's: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. The young man who kept their clothes was afterward made the apostle to the Gentiles.

name: The magistrates of Philippi
text: Beating and imprisoning uncondemned Romans on the word of a mob. The masters of the damsel lost their gains and brought Paul and Silas to the magistrates on a charge about customs. The magistrates rent off their clothes, commanded to beat them, laid many stripes on them and cast them into prison — no trial, no condemnation, and two Roman citizens. In the morning they tried to send them away privily. When her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city, and teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans. The multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them. And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison. They heard no defence and passed no sentence; the mob was the trial. They were made to undo it in person. When it was day the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go; but Paul said, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out. And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans. And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.

name: The seven sons of Sceva
text: Exorcising in the name of Jesus whom Paul preacheth. Vagabond Jewish exorcists at Ephesus, seven sons of a chief priest, took up the name of the Lord Jesus as a formula over those that had evil spirits. The spirit answered, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye? The Name used as a spell by men who did not belong to it, in a city given to curious arts. Taking the name in vain in its most literal form. The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded. Fear fell on the city, the name was magnified, and the practitioners of curious arts burned their books, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth.

name: They that troubled the churches with circumcision
text: Preaching another gospel, subverting souls with a commandment the apostles never gave. Certain men came down from Judea teaching that except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved. The council at Jerusalem disowned them by name — to whom we gave no such commandment — and Paul, writing to Galatia, put them under a curse twice over in two verses. Certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved; and there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses. The apostles' letter names the offense exactly: certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment. In Galatia the same men removed the churches so soon unto another gospel. The sentence is pronounced and repeated: though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed. And to the Galatians: he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be. I would they were even cut off which trouble you.

name: Antipas, Smyrna, and Philadelphia
text: Faithful unto death; keeping the word of his patience; not denying his name in the place where Satan's seat is. Of the seven churches, two are given no rebuke at all, and one man in a third is named by the Lord himself. Smyrna, poor and slandered, is promised a crown of life. Philadelphia, with a little strength, has an open door no man can shut and will be kept from the hour of temptation. Antipas of Pergamos is called my faithful martyr, slain among them where Satan dwelleth. I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich). Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried. Be thou faithful unto death. Thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. Thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death. Behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it. I will make them of the synagogue of Satan to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world. Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown.

name: Barnabas
text: Selling his land and laying the money at the apostles' feet; a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith. A Levite of Cyprus sold his land and brought the whole price to the apostles, in the same chapter and by the same rule that Ananias and Sapphira broke with theirs. He took Saul in when the disciples were afraid of him, went to find him in Tarsus when Antioch needed a teacher, and was the man Antioch's Gentiles first believed under. The apostles named him: the son of consolation. Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Barnabas took Saul, and brought him to the apostles. When he came to Antioch, and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord. For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith. And much people was added unto the Lord. The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them. The Spirit's own naming of him for the first mission to the Gentiles is the blessing; the church's naming of him is the other: son of consolation. His gift and Ananias' lie stand a few verses apart so no one can miss the difference.

name: Cornelius
text: A devout man, one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. A centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea, a Gentile, was praying at the ninth hour when an angel told him his prayers and alms were come up for a memorial before God, and to send for Peter. Peter came, learned on the way that God is no respecter of persons, preached, and the Holy Ghost fell on the whole house before he had finished. They were the first Gentiles baptized. A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house. When Peter came, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet; Peter took him up: I myself also am a man. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God. Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God. Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

name: Dorcas (Tabitha)
text: Full of good works and almsdeeds which she did; the coats and garments she made for the widows. A disciple at Joppa who clothed the widows died, and they washed her and laid her in an upper chamber and sent two men for Peter. When he came, the widows stood by him weeping and showing the coats and garments she had made. He put them out, kneeled, prayed, and said, Tabitha, arise. She opened her eyes, and he presented her alive. Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. All the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them. Her works were her witnesses, and they were held up in the room where she lay. Peter kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up. And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive. And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord. The one woman raised from the dead in the Acts is the one whose alms were in every widow's hands.

name: Gaius, the wellbeloved
text: Walking in the truth; doing faithfully to the brethren and to strangers; bringing them forward on their journey after a godly sort. The third epistle of John is written to him. He kept the travelling brethren, strangers to him, and sent them on their way supplied, and they testified of his charity before the church. In the same short letter Diotrephes is cast out of the church for the opposite. John has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth. Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well: because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth. Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth. For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God.

name: Lydia
text: A seller of purple who worshipped God; whose heart the Lord opened; who constrained the apostles to abide in her house. Paul crossed into Europe on a vision and found no synagogue at Philippi, only women at prayer by the river. One of them, a merchant of Thyatira, heard, believed, was baptized with her household, and would not let the apostles lodge anywhere else. Her house became the church at Philippi, and after the prison and the earthquake it was where Paul and Silas went first. A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us. And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us. Leaving the prison, they entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed. Whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul. The first believer in Europe recorded by name, and the first house of the church that later sent to Paul's necessity once and again, and to which he wrote that he thanked God upon every remembrance of them. The blessing on hospitality is the guests: an apostle and the gospel under her roof.

name: Onesiphorus
text: Oft refreshing Paul, and not ashamed of his chain; seeking him out very diligently in Rome. When everyone in Asia had turned from Paul, one man from Ephesus went to Rome, hunted through the prisons until he found him, and kept coming. Paul's blessing on him is in the last letter he wrote: the Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus, and grant that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day. He oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: but, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me. And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou knowest very well. This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me. The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus. The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day. I was in prison, and ye came unto me: inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Salute the household of Onesiphorus.

name: Paul, at the end of his course
text: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. The man who had held the coats at Stephen's stoning wrote his last letter from a Roman prison, alone except for Luke, with the time of his departure at hand. He gave his own account of himself in one sentence and claimed the crown by name. Before that, five times forty stripes save one, three times beaten with rods, once stoned, three shipwrecks, a night and a day in the deep; and the churches of the Gentiles. For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear. I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel; these hands have ministered unto my necessities. Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. The blessing on Saul of Tarsus, whose own case is his persecution of the church, is written by his own hand at the end of it.

name: Stephen
text: Full of faith and of the Holy Ghost; a face like an angel before the council; forgiving those who stoned him. One of the seven chosen to serve tables, full of faith and power, he did great wonders and out-argued every synagogue that tried him. Accused by suborned witnesses, he preached Abraham to Solomon to a council that stopped their ears and stoned him. He saw heaven opened and the Son of man standing, and asked that the sin not be laid to their charge. A young man named Saul held the coats. Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. All that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel. He, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. The Lord had said, whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God; Stephen saw him stand to do it. Devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him. The blessing recorded is a witness received in heaven in sight of the witness himself, and the persecution that scattered the church to preach the word everywhere, and the coat-holder who became Paul.

name: The Bereans
text: Receiving the word with all readiness of mind, and searching the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. Driven from Thessalonica by a mob, Paul and Silas came to Berea and found a synagogue that did two things at once: welcomed the message and checked it against the scriptures every day. Luke calls them more noble than the Thessalonians for it. Many of them believed, including honourable Greek women and men. These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. They did not believe Paul because he was Paul; they believed the scriptures, and found him in them. Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few. When the Thessalonian Jews came to stir up the city, the brethren sent Paul away, and Silas and Timotheus abode there still. Search the scriptures, Christ had said; the Bereans are the one church named for having done it, and the church was theirs.

name: The Philippian jailer
text: Believing on the Lord with all his house the same night; washing the stripes of the men he had put in the stocks. He thrust Paul and Silas into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks. At midnight they sang, the earthquake opened every door, and he drew his sword to kill himself. Paul cried out that they were all there. He fell down trembling, asked what he must do to be saved, was told, and before dawn had washed their wounds, been baptized with all his house, set meat before them, and rejoiced. Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them. And rejoiced, believing in God with all his house. The prisoners he had chained became his guests, the sword he had drawn on himself went back in its sheath, and the magistrates who had beaten Roman citizens uncondemned came the next morning to beg them to leave. The church at Philippi that Lydia opened her house to had a jailer in it.

name: Timothy, with Lois and Eunice
text: Unfeigned faith that dwelt first in his grandmother and his mother; knowing the holy scriptures from a child. A boy of Lystra with a Greek father and a believing Jewish mother had been taught the scriptures from a child by two women. Paul found him well reported of, circumcised him for the Jews' sake, and took him. He became Paul's own son in the faith, the man he trusted with Ephesus, and the one he wrote his last letter to. When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation. Timotheus was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium. I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state. For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's. But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel. Him would Paul have to go forth with him. Timothy, my own son in the faith. This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. The blessing on the two women's teaching is the man it made: named in the address of six epistles, and left in charge of the church at Ephesus.
